01-01.title: The New Year's Day that gave U2 its first anthem
01-01.story: Bono wrote the lyric imagining Poland's Solidarity movement, but the song started as a bassline Adam Clayton stumbled into while trying to play Visage's 'Fade to Grey'. The Edge's icy piano was a happy accident from a keyboard left in the room.
facts: The band nearly cut the track entirely, convinced it was going nowhere
Bono has said the words came out 'about a couple separated by war' before he knew why

01-02.title: How a broken speaker invented the fuzz guitar
01-02.story: On Marty Robbins' 'Don't Worry', a faulty channel in the studio's mixing console distorted Grady Martin's bass solo into a snarl nobody had heard before. Engineers tried to fix it; the producer kept it.
facts: Nashville session players began requesting 'the broken sound' by name
It led directly to the first commercial fuzz pedal two years later

01-03.title: The drum break that built hip-hop
01-03.story: The Winstons cut 'Amen, Brother' as a B-side throwaway. Its six-second drum break, played by Gregory Coleman in a single take, became the most sampled passage in recorded music.
facts: The break powered entire genres: jungle, drum and bass, and countless hip-hop records
The band saw no royalties from the sampling boom for decades

01-04.title: Why Motown mixed its records on a car speaker
01-04.story: Berry Gordy kept a cheap car-dashboard speaker wired into the Hitsville control room. If a mix didn't hit on that tinny cone, it went back, because that's where America actually heard music.
facts: Engineers called the test 'the Detroit ear'
Motown also boosted mid-range so songs cut through AM radio static

01-05.title: The bassline Paul McCartney built from a mistake
01-05.story: On 'Paperback Writer', McCartney wanted a bass so loud it would rattle radios. Engineer Ken Townsend rigged a loudspeaker as a microphone to capture the low end, a trick no one had tried.
facts: EMI's rulebook technically forbade the setup
The result was the loudest bass ever pressed to a Beatles single to that point

01-06.title: Kraftwerk built their own instruments because none existed
01-06.story: For 'Autobahn', the band constructed custom electronic drums and vocoders in their Kling Klang studio. They were chasing the sound of a car trip, not a band.
facts: The whooshing traffic sounds are synthesized, not recorded
The 22-minute original was cut to three minutes for radio and became a global hit

01-07.title: The piano on 'Layla' was never meant to be there
01-07.story: Drummer Jim Gordon was caught playing a private piano melody during downtime. Eric Clapton heard it through the studio glass and insisted it become the song's second half.
facts: The coda was recorded months after the main track
The two halves were spliced together with tape, not re-performed

01-08.title: Elvis recorded his first single for his mother
01-08.story: At 18, Presley paid Sun Studio's $4 fee to cut 'My Happiness' as a gift. Receptionist Marion Keisker secretly taped a copy because she liked his voice.
facts: Her note read: 'Good ballad singer. Hold.'
That saved tape led Sam Phillips to call him back a year later

01-09.title: Joni Mitchell tuned her guitar wrong on purpose
01-09.story: Polio left Mitchell's left hand weak, so she invented dozens of open tunings that let her voice chords with fewer fingers. Those tunings gave 'Blue' its floating, unplaceable harmony.
facts: She used more than 50 distinct tunings across her career
Guitarists still struggle to cover her songs in standard tuning

01-10.title: The studio trick that made 'Strawberry Fields' impossible
01-10.story: Lennon liked two different takes recorded in different keys at different speeds. George Martin sped one up and slowed the other until they met in the middle.
facts: The splice happens exactly one minute in
Martin later called the odds of it working 'astronomical'

01-11.title: Aretha rewrote 'Respect' and took it from Otis
01-11.story: Otis Redding's original was a man asking for respect at home. Aretha Franklin flipped the perspective, added the spelled-out hook and the 'sock it to me' backing from her sisters.
facts: Redding reportedly said 'that girl has stolen my song'
The R-E-S-P-E-C-T spelling was invented in the studio that day

01-12.title: Why disco records used real strings and a metronome
01-12.story: Philadelphia producers paired full orchestras with a rigid four-on-the-floor kick so DJs could beat-match by hand. The click track was the secret that made mixing possible.
facts: Engineers printed the tempo on the record label for DJs
This is why so many disco 12-inches sit near 120 beats per minute

01-13.title: Brian Eno wrote rules on cards to break writer's block
01-13.story: Frustrated in the studio, Eno printed 'Oblique Strategies' — cards with instructions like 'Honour thy error as a hidden intention'. Musicians drew one when stuck.
facts: Bowie used the deck heavily during the Berlin albums
One card simply reads 'Do nothing for as long as possible'

01-14.title: The Roland TR-808 flopped before it changed everything
01-14.story: Roland discontinued the drum machine after three years because it sounded fake next to real drums. Producers bought them cheap secondhand, and its booming kick became the spine of hip-hop.
facts: The 808's sound came from faulty transistors Roland bought as a batch
When that supply ran out, the machine could not be made again

01-15.title: Stevie Wonder played nearly every instrument on 'Innervisions'
01-15.story: Wonder recorded drums, keys, bass and harmonica himself, layering parts alone in the studio through the night. Engineers worked in shifts to keep up with him.
facts: He often worked 48-hour sessions without leaving
The clavinet sound on 'Higher Ground' was cut in about three hours

01-16.title: Dolly Parton wrote two standards on the same day
01-16.story: Parton has said she wrote 'Jolene' and 'I Will Always Love You' in a single writing session. One was about a bank teller flirting with her husband; the other about leaving her mentor.
facts: Elvis wanted to record 'I Will Always Love You' but his manager demanded publishing
She said no, and kept the rights that later made her a fortune

01-17.title: The Wall of Sound was built by crowding the room
01-17.story: Phil Spector packed multiple pianos, guitars and percussionists into a small echo-heavy studio and recorded them as one blurred mass. The point was density, not clarity.
facts: Musicians played the same part simultaneously to thicken it
The reverb came from a real echo chamber, a concrete room with a speaker

01-18.title: Bob Marley's band recorded in a room with no separation
01-18.story: The Wailers cut early sides live in cramped Kingston studios where every mic bled into the others. That bleed is why the records feel like one breathing organism.
facts: Engineers used the leakage as natural reverb
Bass was cut deliberately loud for Jamaican sound-system playback

01-19.title: Miles Davis handed out no sheet music for 'Kind of Blue'
01-19.story: Davis gave his players only modal sketches minutes before recording. Most of the album is first takes by musicians hearing the material for the first time.
facts: Bill Evans wrote the liner notes comparing it to Japanese brush painting
It remains the best-selling jazz album ever made

01-20.title: Prince played 27 instruments on his debut
01-20.story: Warner Bros. doubted a 19-year-old could produce himself, so Prince recorded a demo playing every part. He got full creative control, almost unheard of for a new artist.
facts: He reportedly recorded the album in about five weeks
His contract made him one of the youngest self-producing artists on a major label

01-21.title: The Fairlight sampler cost as much as a house
01-21.story: The first commercial digital sampler sold for tens of thousands of dollars, limiting it to stars like Kate Bush and Peter Gabriel. It let musicians play any recorded sound from a keyboard.
facts: Bush used it to turn breaking glass into an instrument
Its low memory forced the short, clipped samples that define the era

01-22.title: Why 'Bohemian Rhapsody' took three weeks of overdubs
01-22.story: Queen layered their vocal harmonies up to 180 times, bouncing tape so often it wore thin. Held to the light, the master was nearly transparent.
facts: The band sang 10-12 hours a day for the opera section
No synthesizers were used; the album sleeve said so proudly

01-23.title: Nina Simone trained as a classical pianist, not a singer
01-23.story: Denied a place at the Curtis Institute, Simone took a bar job that required singing. She had only ever intended to play Bach, and that classical phrasing never left her.
facts: Her improvisations often quote Bach fugues mid-song
She sang publicly for the first time only because the club owner insisted

01-24.title: The Clash recorded 'London Calling' with a producer who threw chairs
01-24.story: Guy Stevens motivated takes by swinging ladders and pouring wine on the piano. The chaos was intentional; he wanted performances, not perfection.
facts: Engineer Bill Price quietly kept the tape rolling through the mayhem
The title track's bass was played by Paul Simonon, who learned bass in the band

01-25.title: Hip-hop's first hit used a disco band playing live
01-25.story: 'Rapper's Delight' didn't sample Chic's 'Good Times' — session musicians replayed the groove because sampling technology barely existed.
facts: Chic's Nile Rodgers sued and won a songwriting credit
The record ran nearly 15 minutes on the 12-inch

01-26.title: Sly Stone recorded an album on an early drum machine
01-26.story: For 'There's a Riot Goin' On', Stone used a primitive rhythm box instead of a drummer, then layered tape until the sound smeared. Critics called it murky; he meant it.
facts: He recorded much of it alone in a home studio
The tape was overdubbed so many times the hiss became part of the sound

01-27.title: Mozart's 'Requiem' was finished by someone else
01-27.story: Mozart died leaving the work incomplete. His student Franz Xaver Süssmayr finished it, and his widow hid the fact to secure the commission payment.
facts: Scholars still argue over which bars are actually Mozart's
The anonymous patron wanted to pass it off as his own composition

01-28.title: Robert Johnson recorded facing the corner of a room
01-28.story: In a San Antonio hotel room, Johnson played into the corner. For years it was called superstition; engineers now note it created natural bass reinforcement.
facts: Only 29 songs of his survive
The corner technique is a real acoustic trick still used today

01-29.title: Talking Heads built 'Remain in Light' from loops before loops existed
01-29.story: The band recorded single-bar grooves and spliced them into endless cycles by hand with razor blades and tape, inspired by Fela Kuti's Afrobeat.
facts: Each member recorded parts separately, never playing the song together
Eno and Byrne assembled the arrangements afterward

01-30.title: The Beatles' last live show was on a roof
01-30.story: With no venue and no plan, the band played atop their Savile Row office. London police shut it down after 42 minutes, which is why the film has an ending.
facts: Office workers watched from surrounding rooftops
It was the final time all four performed publicly together

01-31.title: Why reggae's bass sits so far forward
01-31.story: Jamaican records were made for outdoor sound systems where bass carried across a street. Engineers cut low frequencies hot and pulled the treble back.
facts: Producers tested mixes on actual street speakers before release
This is the root of dub, born from stripping vocals off those mixes

02-01.title: Erasmus Hall in Flatbush produced two American icons
02-01.story: Barbra Streisand and Neil Diamond both sang in the chorus at Erasmus Hall High School on Flatbush Avenue, a short walk from Cortelyou Road. They barely knew each other then.
facts: They later recorded the duet 'You Don't Bring Me Flowers' in 1978
Clive Davis, who signed Springsteen and Whitney Houston, also went to Erasmus

02-02.title: The Kings Theatre sat dark for 36 years
02-02.story: The Flatbush Avenue movie palace closed in 1977 and decayed with trees growing through the roof. A restoration reopened it in 2015 as one of Brooklyn's great music rooms.
facts: Original 1929 plasterwork was recast from surviving fragments
It now seats roughly 3,000 for concerts a mile from Ditmas Park

02-03.title: Biggie recorded his debut while still selling on the corner
02-03.story: 'Ready to Die' was cut while Christopher Wallace was living on St. James Place in Clinton Hill. Producers have described him writing nothing down, holding entire verses in his head.
facts: He never used a pen in the booth, a habit Jay-Z also adopted
The album's skits map his actual Brooklyn upbringing

02-04.title: The Beastie Boys started as a Brooklyn hardcore band
02-04.story: Before rapping, the Beastie Boys played fast hardcore punk around New York. Their pivot to hip-hop began as a joke track that got better reactions than their punk set.
facts: Their first release was a hardcore EP, not a rap record
They kept playing instruments themselves long after going platinum

02-05.title: Coney Island's boardwalk had its own sound
02-05.story: Amusement park organs, barkers and competing radios created a dense collage that New York songwriters mined for decades. The Tilyou family's Steeplechase organ was audible for blocks.
facts: Band organs were built to cut through crowd noise without amplification
Brighton Beach's Russian clubs later added a second musical layer nearby

02-06.title: Bob Marley was born on this day
02-06.story: Born in rural Nine Mile, Jamaica, Marley moved to the Kingston slum of Trench Town as a teenager, where the Wailers formed around vocal-group harmony, not roots reggae.
facts: Their earliest records were ska, much faster than what he became known for
He studied welding before committing to music

02-07.title: Brooklyn's Fort Greene birthed a jazz-rap scene
02-07.story: In the early nineties, Fort Greene brownstones hosted a circle of artists that fed groups like Digable Planets and later Black Star's Mos Def and Talib Kweli.
facts: Kweli co-owned Nkiru Books, a Park Slope Black bookstore
Black Star's debut leaned on live jazz samples rather than hard drums

02-08.title: The click track was invented to sync film, not music
02-08.story: Early sound-film composers punched holes in the film itself to make audible clicks, letting orchestras lock to the picture. Recording studios borrowed it decades later.
facts: Musicians initially resisted it as mechanical
Today nearly every pop record is built on a grid descended from it

02-09.title: The Beatles played Ed Sullivan to 73 million people
02-09.story: Broadcast from CBS Studio 50 in Manhattan, the performance was watched by roughly 40 percent of America. Crime rates that hour reportedly dipped.
facts: The studio received 50,000 ticket requests for 700 seats
Sullivan had booked them after seeing fan chaos at Heathrow

02-10.title: Dub was born by accident when a vocal track was left off
02-10.story: Engineer King Tubby pressed a version of a record with the vocals missing. Dancers loved it, so he began deliberately stripping tracks and drenching them in echo.
facts: He rewired mixing desks by hand to create his effects
Dub's remix logic is the direct ancestor of electronic dance music

02-11.title: Whitney Houston's mother sang backup for Aretha
02-11.story: Cissy Houston led the Sweet Inspirations, who sang behind Aretha Franklin and Elvis. Whitney grew up in studios watching that work.
facts: Dionne Warwick is her cousin
Cissy also sang on Van Morrison's 'Brown Eyed Girl' sessions era material

02-12.title: Handel wrote 'Messiah' in 24 days
02-12.story: Working almost without sleep, Handel completed the 259-page score in just over three weeks. A servant reported finding him weeping at his desk.
facts: It premiered in Dublin, not London
Audiences were asked to leave hoops and swords at home to fit more people in

02-13.title: The 'Loud War' shrank music's dynamic range
02-13.story: Mastering engineers began compressing records to sound louder than competitors on radio and CD changers. The side effect was flattened peaks and listening fatigue.
facts: Some nineties reissues are quieter than their originals by design
Streaming loudness normalization has since reduced the incentive

02-14.title: Ol' Dirty Bastard was born in Fort Greene
02-14.story: Russell Jones grew up in Brooklyn and took his stage name from a kung-fu film, claiming there was 'no father to his style'. His off-key delivery was deliberate.
facts: He was cousins with RZA and GZA of Wu-Tang
His vocal takes were often recorded in one pass with no punch-ins

02-15.title: Nat King Cole was a pianist first
02-15.story: Cole led an influential piano trio for years before singing became his main draw. He only sang because a club patron demanded it, by his own account.
facts: His trio format dropped drums, unusual for the era
He was among the first Black artists to host a national TV show

02-16.title: Barclays Center changed which artists tour Brooklyn
02-16.story: Before 2012, most arena acts skipped Brooklyn entirely for Manhattan or the Meadowlands. The Atlantic Avenue arena reversed that overnight.
facts: Jay-Z played the opening eight-night run
It sits atop one of the busiest transit hubs in the borough

02-17.title: Autotune was invented by an oil industry engineer
02-17.story: Andy Hildebrand used seismic data math, designed to find oil underground, to detect and correct pitch. He built it as a subtle repair tool.
facts: Cher's 'Believe' used the extreme setting the inventor called a joke
Hildebrand said he never expected anyone to use it that way

02-18.title: Yoko Ono and John Lennon recorded a heartbeat
02-18.story: Their experimental albums included a recording of their unborn child's heartbeat, followed by silence after the pregnancy was lost. Few records have been that raw.
facts: Critics dismissed the work at the time
It anticipated decades of sound-art practice

02-19.title: Smokey Robinson wrote the song Motown almost rejected
02-19.story: 'The Tracks of My Tears' came from a guitar figure Marv Tarplin played for weeks before lyrics existed. Robinson wrote to the guitar, not the other way around.
facts: Bob Dylan reportedly called Robinson America's greatest living poet
The guitar intro was kept exactly as Tarplin first improvised it

02-20.title: Kurt Cobain was born, and later hid melodies in noise
02-20.story: Cobain's writing method paired sweet pop melody with deliberately abrasive tone, a tension he credited to loving both the Beatles and Black Flag.
facts: 'Nevermind' was mixed to sound more polished than the band wanted
He wrote lyrics minutes before recording many vocals

02-21.title: Nina Simone played Carnegie Hall, but not as she planned
02-21.story: When Simone finally reached Carnegie Hall, she noted bitterly that she arrived as a pop singer, not the classical concert pianist she trained to be.
facts: She opened sets with Bach preludes to make the point
Her civil-rights songs cost her radio play and income

02-22.title: Flatbush's Caribbean records shaped Brooklyn radio
02-22.story: Waves of Caribbean migration made Flatbush a hub for calypso, soca and reggae pressings. Local record shops imported Jamaican dubplates before mainstream stores carried them.
facts: Sound systems set up in backyards and church halls across the neighborhood
That circuit fed directly into New York hip-hop's early sound

02-23.title: George Frideric Handel went blind writing music
02-23.story: Handel continued composing and performing after losing his sight, dictating revisions from memory. Audiences reported he still improvised organ solos flawlessly.
facts: He was buried in Westminster Abbey with 3,000 mourners
His late oratorios were largely written without being able to see the page

02-24.title: The Sugarhill Gang were not a real group
02-24.story: Label owner Sylvia Robinson assembled three unknowns after hearing rap at a party. One was auditioned while working at a pizzeria.
facts: Big Bank Hank reportedly borrowed rhymes from Grandmaster Caz
Caz received no credit or royalties for lines used on the record

02-25.title: George Harrison's sitar lesson changed rock
02-25.story: Harrison studied under Ravi Shankar, who insisted he learn properly rather than use the instrument as decoration. Indian modes then filtered into Western pop.
facts: Shankar initially had no idea who the Beatles were
'Within You Without You' features no other Beatle

02-26.title: Fats Domino sold more records than anyone but Elvis
02-26.story: The New Orleans pianist's rolling triplets defined early rock piano. He recorded almost everything at Cosimo Matassa's tiny J&M studio.
facts: The studio was in the back of an appliance shop
Its cramped room created the signature slapback sound

02-27.title: Brooklyn's Prospect Park bandshell started a free summer tradition
02-27.story: Celebrate Brooklyn began as a modest neighborhood series and grew into one of America's longest-running free outdoor festivals, minutes from Ditmas Park.
facts: It launched partly to bring people back into the park after a rough decade
Acts range from Afrobeat legends to local Brooklyn bands

02-28.title: The Moog synthesizer needed a hit to be taken seriously
02-28.story: Wendy Carlos's 'Switched-On Bach' proved the Moog could make music, not just noise. It became one of the best-selling classical records ever.
facts: Each note had to be played and layered one at a time
The instrument was monophonic, so chords required many passes

02-29.title: Leap day gave Gioachino Rossini a rare birthday
02-29.story: Born on 29 February, Rossini joked he only aged once every four years. He retired from opera at 37 and spent decades writing small pieces and cooking.
facts: He wrote 'The Barber of Seville' in about three weeks
He named several compositions after food

03-01.title: Chopin and the piano that never left the room
03-01.story: Chopin wrote almost exclusively for solo piano, rarely performing in large halls because his playing was too quiet. He preferred salons of a few dozen listeners.
facts: He gave roughly 30 public concerts in his entire life
His pupils described his rubato as 'the tree keeps time, the leaves sway'

03-02.title: Lou Reed recorded an album designed to be unlistenable
03-02.story: 'Metal Machine Music' was 64 minutes of guitar feedback. Reed said it was sincere; the label suspected he was escaping a contract.
facts: It was returned by buyers in enormous numbers
Decades later, an ensemble performed it as scored contemporary music

03-03.title: 'The Star-Spangled Banner' was set to a drinking song
03-03.story: Francis Scott Key's poem was matched to 'To Anacreon in Heaven', a British social club tune notorious for its difficult octave-and-a-half range.
facts: That range is why singers so often struggle with it
It became the official anthem only in 1931

03-04.title: Antonio Vivaldi taught music at an orphanage
03-04.story: Vivaldi spent decades directing music at a Venetian institution for abandoned girls. Much of his catalogue was written for those young musicians.
facts: Visitors traveled to Venice specifically to hear them play
His works were largely forgotten until a 20th-century revival

03-05.title: The Notorious B.I.G. was killed at 24
03-05.story: Wallace died in Los Angeles weeks before releasing 'Life After Death'. Brooklyn responded with an impromptu street procession through Bed-Stuy.
facts: His funeral procession drew thousands to Fulton Street
Brooklyn later co-named a block Christopher Wallace Way

03-06.title: Sampling law changed because of one bass note
03-06.story: A court ruled that even a two-second sample required clearance, forcing producers to either pay or replay parts. Entire production styles became legally impossible.
facts: Records like 'Paul's Boutique' could not be cleared today
Producers pivoted to live replays and original loops

03-07.title: Maurice Ravel wrote 'Boléro' as an experiment in repetition
03-07.story: Ravel called it 'orchestral tissue without music', a single melody repeated with growing instrumentation and no development. He was surprised it became famous.
facts: The snare drum plays the same rhythm for roughly 15 minutes
He reportedly said the piece contained 'no music in it whatsoever'

03-08.title: Jay-Z grew up in Marcy Houses
03-08.story: Shawn Carter's Bed-Stuy childhood is stitched through his catalogue. Like Biggie, he famously records without writing lyrics down.
facts: He founded Roc-A-Fella after labels passed on signing him
Marcy Houses appears by name across three decades of his songs

03-09.title: Ella Fitzgerald invented her scat by copying horns
03-09.story: Fitzgerald built solos by imitating trumpet and saxophone lines rather than singing words, turning her voice into a brass instrument.
facts: She could reproduce bebop solos note for note
Her 'Songbook' series helped canonize American standards

03-10.title: The first commercial radio broadcast changed listening forever
03-10.story: Early stations discovered that recorded music filled airtime cheaply. Within a decade, radio play, not sheet music, determined what became a hit.
facts: Sheet music sales collapsed as radio grew
Record labels initially fought radio, fearing it would kill sales

03-11.title: Bobby McFerrin used no instruments at all
03-11.story: 'Don't Worry, Be Happy' is entirely voice and body percussion, multitracked. Listeners assumed they were hearing a full band.
facts: Every sound including the bass is McFerrin's own voice
It was the first a cappella song to top the US chart

03-12.title: Ditmas Park's Victorian porches became rehearsal rooms
03-12.story: The freestanding wooden houses around Cortelyou Road gave Brooklyn musicians something rare: space to make noise. Porch sessions became an informal neighborhood circuit.
facts: The district holds one of the largest concentrations of Victorian homes in America
Local house concerts still run on the same blocks

03-13.title: Neil Diamond wrote hits in a Brill Building cubicle
03-13.story: Before stardom, the Brooklyn-born Diamond wrote songs for hire in a tiny Manhattan office with a piano and a chair, competing with dozens of writers per floor.
facts: He grew up in Brooklyn and attended Erasmus Hall
'I'm a Believer' was written as work-for-hire and became a Monkees hit

03-14.title: Quincy Jones arranged for Sinatra at 29
03-14.story: Jones's charts gave Sinatra's Basie-era records their swing. He later moved from jazz arranging to producing the best-selling album in history.
facts: He began as a trumpeter touring with Lionel Hampton
He produced 'Thriller' two decades later

03-15.title: Sister Rosetta Tharpe played electric guitar before Chuck Berry
03-15.story: Tharpe's distorted gospel guitar and showmanship directly shaped rock and roll. Berry, Presley and Little Richard all cited her.
facts: She played a solid-body electric in churches, scandalizing congregations
She was inducted into the Rock Hall only in 2018

03-16.title: The Ramones played 2:30 songs to fit more into a set
03-16.story: Their debut cost about $6,400 and ran under 30 minutes. Speed and brevity were economic decisions as much as aesthetic ones.
facts: They counted off every song identically
The whole album was recorded in about a week

03-17.title: Nas recorded 'Illmatic' with four different producers
03-17.story: Rather than one house sound, Nas invited DJ Premier, Pete Rock, Q-Tip and Large Professor. The album runs under 40 minutes with no filler.
facts: He was 20 when it was released
Its brevity was deliberate; he cut anything that repeated an idea

03-18.title: John Coltrane practiced until his lips bled
03-18.story: Bandmates described Coltrane practicing 12 hours a day, sometimes falling asleep with the horn in his mouth. 'Giant Steps' came from that obsession.
facts: Its chord changes are still a rite of passage for jazz students
Pianist Tommy Flanagan sight-read the session and struggled famously

03-19.title: Wagner built a theater to control how his music was heard
03-19.story: Frustrated by noisy houses, Wagner designed Bayreuth with a hidden orchestra pit and a darkened hall, inventing conventions concert audiences still follow.
facts: Darkening the auditorium was considered radical
The sunken pit blends the orchestra into a single sound

03-20.title: The first rap record label ran out of a New Jersey house
03-20.story: Sugar Hill Records began as a family operation with a house band and minimal equipment, pressing records faster than major labels could react.
facts: Sylvia Robinson had been a hit singer herself in the fifties
Majors dismissed rap as a novelty for years

03-21.title: Bach was jailed for trying to quit his job
03-21.story: Bach spent nearly a month in detention after asking too insistently to leave a court position. He kept composing during his confinement.
facts: He fathered 20 children, several becoming composers
Much of his music was unpublished at his death

03-22.title: Brooklyn's Fania sound made salsa a global export
03-22.story: Fania Records' live shows, many featuring Brooklyn and Bronx players, turned New York salsa into an international movement.
facts: Their Yankee Stadium concert ended when fans rushed the field
Brooklyn's Puerto Rican and Dominican communities were core to the scene

03-23.title: Kate Bush choreographed her own videos to tell the story
03-23.story: Trained in mime and dance, Bush treated the promo video as performance art at a time when most artists simply lip-synced.
facts: She was 19 when 'Wuthering Heights' topped the UK chart
She wrote it after catching the last 10 minutes of a TV adaptation

03-24.title: The Wrecking Crew played on records credited to bands
03-24.story: A pool of Los Angeles session musicians performed on hits attributed to famous groups. Many listeners never knew.
facts: Carol Kaye played bass on hundreds of well-known records
Some bands only learned their own parts after release

03-25.title: Aretha Franklin was born, and learned in her father's church
03-25.story: Franklin grew up singing gospel in Detroit under her preacher father, absorbing a call-and-response phrasing she never abandoned in secular music.
facts: She played piano on many of her own recordings
Her Atlantic breakthrough came after Columbia tried to make her a pop crooner

03-26.title: Pink Floyd recorded a heartbeat to open an album
03-26.story: 'The Dark Side of the Moon' opens with a treated bass drum simulating a pulse, then loops of interviews with studio staff answering existential questions.
facts: Paul McCartney was interviewed but his answers were unused
The album charted for over 900 weeks

03-27.title: Mariah Carey co-wrote nearly everything she sang
03-27.story: Unusual for a young pop signing, Carey held writing credits from her debut, giving her long-term control of her catalogue.
facts: She uses the whistle register, a rare vocal extreme
Her demo reached a label head at a party by chance

03-28.title: Brooklyn's Bushwick lofts became a DIY venue circuit
03-28.story: Cheap industrial space turned into all-ages venues run without licenses, incubating a generation of indie bands before rents rose.
facts: Many were shut down over fire-code violations
The circuit launched acts that later headlined Barclays Center

03-29.title: The theremin is played without being touched
03-29.story: Leon Theremin's instrument responds to hand position in an electromagnetic field. It requires perfect pitch because there is nothing to feel.
facts: Lenin personally tried playing it
It later gave science-fiction film its signature eerie tone

03-30.title: Tracy Chapman's breakthrough happened by accident
03-30.story: When Stevie Wonder's gear failed at a televised benefit, Chapman was sent back out alone with a guitar. Her album sales exploded within days.
facts: She played 'Fast Car' to an audience of hundreds of millions
She had been busking in Boston a few years earlier

03-31.title: Marvin Gaye had to fight his label to release 'What's Going On'
03-31.story: Berry Gordy called the record uncommercial and refused to put it out. Gaye went on strike until Motown relented, and it became their landmark album.
facts: Gordy later admitted he was wrong
The overlapping party chatter was recorded at a real gathering

04-01.title: The 'Funky Drummer' break that built a thousand hits
04-01.story: Clyde Stubblefield's drum break on James Brown's 'Funky Drummer' was improvised filler. It became one of the most sampled recordings in history.
facts: Public Enemy, Run-DMC, LL Cool J and George Michael all used it
Stubblefield was never paid sampling royalties and said he didn't mind the music, only the credit

hits: LL Cool J - Mama Said Knock You Out

04-02.title: Which 'Respect' wins: Otis or Aretha?
04-02.story: Otis Redding wrote it in 1965 as a working man's plea. Aretha Franklin rebuilt it in 1967 as a demand, adding the spelling hook and her sisters' backing vocals.
facts: Redding joked she had stolen the song for good
Aretha's version was cut in a single afternoon session

04-03.title: Nile Rodgers' guitar is on more hits than you think
04-03.story: The Chic guitarist's clipped 'chucking' style powered his own band, then Bowie's 'Let's Dance', Madonna's 'Like a Virgin' and Daft Punk's 'Get Lucky'.
facts: He uses a 1960 Stratocaster he calls 'The Hitmaker'
He and Bernard Edwards wrote Sister Sledge's catalogue too

04-04.title: Marvin Gaye's 'Inner City Blues' hid a second bassline
04-04.story: Bassist Bob Babbitt and James Jamerson both appear across the album, and Gaye layered a second bass an octave apart to thicken the low end.
facts: Jamerson famously recorded lying flat on his back
He played most parts with a single index finger, nicknamed 'The Hook'

04-05.title: The Amen break is six seconds long and built three genres
04-05.story: Chopped and sped up, the Winstons' break became the engine of jungle, drum and bass and UK hardcore, often at double its original tempo.
facts: Producers slice it into individual hits and rebuild new patterns
A crowdfunding campaign later raised money for the surviving band member

hits: Oasis - D'You Know What I Mean?

04-06.title: Which 'Hallelujah' wins: Cohen or Buckley?
04-06.story: Leonard Cohen wrote around 80 verses and released a restrained gospel-tinged version. Jeff Buckley's 1994 reading, learned from John Cale's cover, made it a standard.
facts: Cohen spent years writing it, reportedly banging his head on a hotel floor
Buckley's take is a single guitar and voice, recorded largely live

04-07.title: Billie Holiday recorded a protest song no label would touch
04-07.story: Columbia refused 'Strange Fruit', so Holiday cut it for tiny Commodore Records. Clubs made her close with it, lights out, no encore.
facts: The lyric began as a poem by a Bronx schoolteacher
She said singing it made her physically ill every time

04-08.title: Brooklyn's Bed-Stuy gave hip-hop its densest block
04-08.story: Within a few square blocks, Big Daddy Kane, Jay-Z, Biggie, Lil' Kim and Masta Ace all emerged, a concentration unmatched anywhere.
facts: Kane's rapid-fire delivery set the technical bar for the era
Local park jams were the proving ground before any label interest

04-09.title: Rick Rubin produced by taking things away
04-09.story: Rubin's method was subtraction: strip the arrangement until only the essential remains. He applied it to Run-DMC, Slayer, Johnny Cash and Adele.
facts: He often cannot play any instrument on the records he makes
His Def Jam label started in an NYU dorm room

04-10.title: 'Under Pressure' was a jam nobody planned
04-10.story: Bowie and Queen were in the same Swiss studio and started improvising. The famous bassline came from John Deacon noodling during a break.
facts: Accounts differ on who actually invented the riff
Vanilla Ice later used it and initially denied the resemblance

04-11.title: Which 'I Will Always Love You' wins: Dolly or Whitney?
04-11.story: Dolly Parton wrote it as a quiet goodbye to her mentor. Whitney Houston's 1992 version added the a cappella opening that producer David Foster fought for.
facts: Parton has said she cried hearing Whitney's version on the radio
The a cappella intro was nearly cut for being too risky

04-12.title: The 'Think' break gave hip-hop its whistle
04-12.story: Lyn Collins' 'Think (About It)', produced by James Brown, supplied the 'woo! yeah!' stabs heard on hundreds of records.
facts: Rob Base and DJ E-Z Rock built an entire hit on it
The vocal stabs are now shorthand for party records

04-13.title: Carole King wrote hits in Brooklyn before singing them
04-13.story: Born in Manhattan and raised in Brooklyn, King wrote dozens of standards with Gerry Goffin before 'Tapestry' made her a performer.
facts: She attended James Madison High School in Brooklyn
'Will You Love Me Tomorrow' was written when she was 17

04-14.title: Bernie Worrell made the synthesizer funky
04-14.story: Parliament-Funkadelic's keyboardist treated the Moog as a bass instrument, inventing the squelching low end that shaped G-funk two decades later.
facts: He was classically trained and wrote a concerto as a child
Dr. Dre's nineties productions lean directly on his vocabulary

04-15.title: Which 'Tainted Love' wins: Gloria Jones or Soft Cell?
04-15.story: Gloria Jones cut a fast Northern Soul stomper that flopped. Soft Cell slowed it to a synth crawl in 1981 and had a worldwide hit.
facts: The song was a UK club favourite for years before the cover
Soft Cell's version keeps the melody but inverts the energy entirely

04-16.title: Dub plates were one-off records made for a single night
04-16.story: Sound systems cut exclusive acetates so rivals could not play their tunes. The discs wore out after a few dozen plays.
facts: Exclusivity, not fidelity, was the point
The practice migrated to UK garage and grime decades later

04-17.title: 'Superstition' began as a gift to a guitarist
04-17.story: Stevie Wonder wrote the clavinet riff for Jeff Beck. When Motown heard it, they insisted Wonder keep it, straining the friendship.
facts: Wonder played drums, clavinet and moog bass himself
Beck did record a version, but it came out after Wonder's

04-18.title: The producer who never let artists hear playback
04-18.story: Phil Spector often refused to let performers hear the full mix, keeping the arrangement in his head so no one could argue with it.
facts: Sessions ran for hours with dozens of players
Darlene Love's voice appeared on records credited to other groups

04-19.title: 'Apache' is called the national anthem of hip-hop
04-19.story: The Incredible Bongo Band's cover gave DJs a long percussion break perfect for cutting between two turntables.
facts: Kool Herc played it at Bronx block parties
The break is essentially a drum solo with congas

hits: LL Cool J - You Can't Dance

04-20.title: Luther Vandross sang jingles before he sang ballads
04-20.story: Vandross earned a living singing commercials and backing vocals for Bowie and Chic before launching a solo career.
facts: He arranged the backing vocals on Bowie's 'Young Americans'
He sang on ads for soft drinks and fast food chains

04-21.title: Prince died, leaving a vault of unreleased music
04-21.story: Prince recorded relentlessly, storing thousands of unreleased tracks in a bank-style vault at Paisley Park. Estimates suggest decades of material.
facts: He often recorded alone overnight, engineering himself
Some vault songs date to the seventies

04-22.title: Which 'Girls Just Want to Have Fun' wins: Hazard or Lauper?
04-22.story: Robert Hazard wrote it from a man's perspective as a demo. Cyndi Lauper rewrote the meaning entirely, turning it into a feminist anthem.
facts: Lauper initially disliked the song and refused to record it
She rewrote lyrics to flip the point of view

04-23.title: Ray Charles fused gospel and blues and offended both
04-23.story: 'I Got a Woman' set secular lyrics to a gospel structure. Churches called it sacrilege; it also invented soul music.
facts: He rewrote an existing gospel song's changes
Radio programmers were unsure which format it belonged to

04-24.title: Kool Herc invented the breakbeat at a Bronx party
04-24.story: Herc noticed dancers waited for the drum break, so he used two copies of a record to loop it indefinitely. Hip-hop starts there.
facts: He called it the 'merry-go-round' technique
The party was a back-to-school fundraiser for his sister

04-25.title: Ella and Louis recorded almost entirely live
04-25.story: Their duet albums were cut with both singers in the room, no overdubs, letting the timing breathe imperfectly on purpose.
facts: Producer Norman Granz kept takes with audible laughter
The rhythm section was Oscar Peterson's trio

04-26.title: Grandmaster Flash built his mixer by hand
04-26.story: Trained in electronics, Flash rigged a crossfader and cue system so he could hear the next record before the crowd did.
facts: He soldered parts salvaged from junked stereos
That preview capability made beat-matching possible

04-27.title: 'Change the Beat' gave the world its most-scratched sound
04-27.story: The 'ahhh, fresh' vocoder phrase at the end of Fab 5 Freddy's record became the single most-scratched sample in DJ history.
facts: It was recorded almost as an afterthought at the session's end
Nearly every turntablist routine still uses it

04-28.title: Ann Peebles wrote a hit about wanting bad weather
04-28.story: 'I Can't Stand the Rain' came from an offhand complaint about going out in a storm. Her co-writers turned the line into the hook on the spot.
facts: John Lennon called it the best song he'd ever heard
The opening electric timbale imitates falling rain

04-29.title: Duke Ellington wrote for specific players, not instruments
04-29.story: Ellington composed around individual musicians' quirks, writing parts only they could play. Replacing a member meant rewriting the music.
facts: He called his orchestra his real instrument
He wrote on trains between gigs for decades

04-30.title: The Ditmas Park porch concert circuit
04-30.story: Neighbors around Cortelyou Road turned Victorian porches into micro-venues, hosting acoustic sets for audiences of thirty. The tradition continues each summer.
facts: Some porches host annual multi-act bills
The format traces back to house-party culture across Flatbush

05-01.title: 'Sunshine of Your Love' came from a bass riff heard at a gig
05-01.story: Jack Bruce wrote the riff after seeing Jimi Hendrix play live and going home to his bass at dawn.
facts: Ginger Baker's tom pattern was inspired by Native American rhythms
The band nearly rejected it as too simple

05-02.title: Which 'Blinded by the Light' wins: Springsteen or Manfred Mann?
05-02.story: Springsteen's original is a wordy folk-rock rush. Manfred Mann's Earth Band slowed it, changed a lyric and scored the only Springsteen-written US number one.
facts: Springsteen has joked he never had a chart-topper with his own version
The famous misheard lyric comes from Mann's rewrite

05-03.title: James Jamerson never wrote his basslines down
05-03.story: Motown's uncredited bassist improvised most parts on first take. Because nothing was notated, many lines were lost when he died.
facts: He appears on more number ones than the Beatles and Elvis combined
He was not credited on album sleeves for most of his career

05-04.title: 'Sing Sing' delivered the drums for a hip-hop decade
05-04.story: Gaz's 'Sing Sing' and its cousins supplied breaks that New York DJs guarded like secrets, soaking labels off records to hide titles.
facts: DJs soaked or scratched off labels to protect their sources
Digging culture grew directly from that secrecy

05-05.title: Bo Diddley built his own rectangular guitars
05-05.story: Diddley designed square-bodied guitars because standard shapes were awkward when he jumped around on stage. His clave-derived rhythm became a genre unto itself.
facts: The 'Bo Diddley beat' underpins hundreds of rock songs
He built early guitars himself in a workshop

05-06.title: Sam Cooke wrote 'A Change Is Gonna Come' after hearing Dylan
05-06.story: Cooke was struck that a white songwriter had written 'Blowin' in the Wind' before he had written anything like it, and responded within months.
facts: He was nervous performing it live, calling it too personal
The string arrangement was unusually cinematic for R&B

05-07.title: 'La Di Da Di' is a rap record with no instruments
05-07.story: Doug E. Fresh beatboxed the entire backing track while Slick Rick rapped over it. Nothing else appears on the recording.
facts: It has been sampled on hundreds of songs
Snoop Dogg rebuilt an entire track from its lyrics

extra.src: Doug E. Fresh & Slick Rick - La Di Da Di (1985)

05-08.title: Robert Moog never intended to build a music instrument
05-08.story: Moog was a theremin hobbyist and engineer who built modules to order. Musicians told him what they needed and the synthesizer emerged.
facts: The keyboard was added because players asked for one
He said he thought of himself as a toolmaker, not a musician

05-09.title: Which 'Nothing Compares 2 U' wins: Prince or Sinéad?
05-09.story: Prince wrote it for his side project The Family. Sinéad O'Connor's 1990 version, with its single-shot video, became definitive.
facts: Her tears in the video were reportedly unplanned
Prince rarely performed it before her version succeeded

05-10.title: Bo Hansson and the rise of the bedroom studio
05-10.story: Long before home recording was normal, musicians began assembling private studios, shifting power away from label-owned rooms.
facts: Multitrack tape became affordable in the seventies
This lineage runs directly to laptop production today

05-11.title: Bob Marley survived being shot and played two days later
05-11.story: Gunmen wounded Marley at his Kingston home before a peace concert. He performed anyway, showing the crowd his injured arm.
facts: He said 'the people who are trying to make this world worse aren't taking a day off'
He left Jamaica for London shortly after

05-12.title: The Winstons' break has its own documentary
05-12.story: Decades after 'Amen, Brother', filmmakers traced how six seconds spawned entire scenes without the band's knowledge or payment.
facts: Copyright never protected the drummer's performance itself
Public fundraising eventually delivered some belated compensation

05-13.title: Stevie Wonder's harmonica part was a first take
05-13.story: 'Fingertips' captured a 12-year-old improvising live, including a bassist audibly asking 'What key? What key?' as the band scrambled.
facts: That confused shout is on the released record
It became Motown's first live number one

05-14.title: Sister Nancy's 'Bam Bam' is reggae's most reused hook
05-14.story: Recorded quickly over an existing riddim, it became one of the most sampled Jamaican records ever, though she saw little income for decades.
facts: She discovered her song in a film only by chance
She later won back rights to her recording

05-15.title: Brooklyn's Coney Island Baby and the doo-wop corners
05-15.story: Street-corner harmony groups rehearsed in Brooklyn subway entrances and hallways for the natural reverb, an early form of free studio time.
facts: Tiled stairwells acted as echo chambers
Groups auditioned by singing under overpasses

05-16.title: Which 'Mr. Tambourine Man' wins: Dylan or The Byrds?
05-16.story: Dylan's original is a long acoustic reverie. The Byrds cut it to two and a half minutes with a 12-string Rickenbacker and invented folk-rock.
facts: Only one Byrd actually played on the recording
Session players filled in the rest

05-17.title: Bill Withers was making toilet seats for airplanes
05-17.story: Withers kept his factory job while recording 'Ain't No Sunshine', assuming music would not last. The famous repeated 'I know' was a placeholder.
facts: He meant to write real lyrics there but was told to keep it
He brought his lunchbox to the studio

05-18.title: Delia Derbyshire realized the Doctor Who theme with tape
05-18.story: Working without synthesizers, Derbyshire built the theme by recording single tones, cutting the tape and splicing pitches by hand.
facts: Each note was measured with a ruler
She received no on-screen composer credit for years

05-19.title: 'Impeach the President' gave hip-hop its snare
05-19.story: The Honey Drippers' record, cut by a high-school band, contains a drum intro that became a foundation of nineties New York production.
facts: Its snare defines much of the boom-bap era
The players were teenagers when they recorded it

extra.src: The Honey Drippers - Impeach the President (1973)
hits: Janet Jackson - That's the Way Love Goes

05-20.title: Bach's music was rescued by a butcher's wrapping paper
05-20.story: Legend holds Mendelssohn found Bach manuscripts used as packing material, sparking the revival that restored Bach to the canon.
facts: He staged the St Matthew Passion after 100 years of neglect
Bach was known mainly as an organist in his lifetime

05-21.title: The Bomb Squad layered dozens of samples per track
05-21.story: Public Enemy's producers stacked sirens, horn stabs and drums into deliberately abrasive collages, a technique legally impossible today.
facts: Some tracks contain over 20 distinct sources
Clearance costs would now exceed any budget

05-22.title: 'Trans-Europe Express' became the spine of electro
05-22.story: Afrika Bambaataa built 'Planet Rock' on Kraftwerk's melody and a TR-808, connecting Düsseldorf to the Bronx.
facts: Kraftwerk's label pursued the matter afterward
The record effectively created electro as a genre

05-23.title: Rosetta Tharpe played a train station gig
05-23.story: Promoters staged a concert on a disused British railway platform with the audience across the tracks. Tharpe arrived by carriage and played in the rain.
facts: The footage became one of her best-known performances
She improvised through a downpour without stopping

05-24.title: Bob Dylan went electric and got booed
05-24.story: At Newport, Dylan plugged in and split the folk audience. The hostility followed him across a world tour.
facts: A famous heckler shouted 'Judas' in Manchester
He responded by telling the band to play louder

05-25.title: Miles Davis plugged in and lost half his audience
05-25.story: 'Bitches Brew' used electric instruments and studio editing, alienating purists while inventing fusion.
facts: Producer Teo Macero spliced the tapes like a film editor
Long passages were assembled, not performed continuously

05-26.title: Which 'Killing Me Softly' wins: Flack or the Fugees?
05-26.story: Roberta Flack's version is intimate and slow. The Fugees rebuilt it in 1996 over a hip-hop break with Lauryn Hill's lead.
facts: Flack publicly praised the remake
The Fugees kept the melody almost unchanged

05-27.title: Brooklyn's Fulton Street record shops fed the DJs
05-27.story: Independent shops along Fulton and Flatbush stocked breaks, imports and white labels that defined what Brooklyn DJs could play.
facts: Shop owners often acted as informal A&R
Many crews formed in the aisles

05-28.title: Gladys Knight had the first 'Grapevine' hit, then lost it
05-28.story: Gladys Knight and the Pips charted with 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine' before Marvin Gaye's slower version eclipsed it entirely.
facts: Motown shelved Gaye's take for over a year
Gaye's version became the label's biggest-selling single to that point

05-29.title: Stravinsky's premiere caused a riot
05-29.story: 'The Rite of Spring' provoked shouting and fistfights at its Paris debut. The dancers could not hear the orchestra over the noise.
facts: The choreographer shouted counts from the wings
It is now standard repertoire worldwide

05-30.title: The SP-1200 forced producers to be brief
05-30.story: The sampler held only about ten seconds of audio, so producers chopped tightly and sped samples up, creating a gritty sound now sought deliberately.
facts: Its 12-bit conversion added the crunch producers loved
Modern plugins emulate its limitations on purpose

05-31.title: 'Ashley's Roachclip' hid a break at the very end
05-31.story: The Soul Searchers buried a drum break near the track's close, which producers found decades later and used everywhere.
facts: Digging often meant listening to full albums for seconds of usable audio
The break drives one of the biggest pop hits of the eighties

hits: Eric B. & Rakim - Paid in Full
Milli Vanilli - Girl You Know It's True
PM Dawn - Set Adrift on Memory Bliss

06-01.title: Marilyn Monroe's birthday and the art of the breathy mic
06-01.story: Close-mic crooning only became possible with sensitive condenser microphones, letting singers whisper instead of project.
facts: Before electric mics, singers needed opera-level volume
The intimate vocal style is a technology story as much as a taste one

06-02.title: Charlie Watts kept time by leaving the hi-hat out
06-02.story: The Rolling Stones drummer lifted his hi-hat hand on backbeats, a jazz habit that gave the band its slight, distinctive drag.
facts: He considered himself a jazz drummer his whole life
That tiny gap is why Stones grooves feel loose

06-03.title: Which 'Twist and Shout' wins: Isley Brothers or Beatles?
06-03.story: The Isley Brothers cut the definitive early version. Lennon recorded the Beatles' take last on a session day with a shredded throat.
facts: Lennon's voice gave out immediately afterward
It was done in one take because he could not sing another

06-04.title: Cecil Taylor turned the piano into percussion
06-04.story: Taylor attacked the keyboard with clusters and forearms, treating it as 88 tuned drums rather than a melodic instrument.
facts: He trained classically at conservatory
Audiences frequently walked out of early performances

06-05.title: Bill Withers recorded 'Grandma's Hands' in under two minutes
06-05.story: Withers wrote about his grandmother's church in West Virginia. The song is barely 120 seconds long and needed nothing more.
facts: Blackstreet later built 'No Diggity' on its bones
He resisted adding a bridge, saying it was finished

06-06.title: Prince Buster shaped the beat that became ska
06-06.story: Buster instructed guitarists to accent the offbeat, flipping Jamaican R&B into ska and eventually rocksteady and reggae.
facts: He staged sound-system clashes as public theatre
Two-tone bands in Britain rebuilt his catalogue

06-07.title: Prince changed his name to a symbol to escape a contract
06-07.story: In a dispute with Warner Bros., Prince adopted an unpronounceable glyph and wrote 'slave' on his face at appearances.
facts: Media resorted to calling him 'the artist formerly known as'
Floppy disks with the symbol font were mailed to press

06-08.title: Brooklyn's Kings Theatre reopening drew a Flatbush crowd
06-08.story: After decades dark, the Flatbush palace reopened with a sold-out show, restoring a major venue to the neighborhood's doorstep.
facts: Restoration took roughly four years
It is among the largest theaters in Brooklyn

06-09.title: Les Paul invented multitrack recording in his garage
06-09.story: Frustrated by one-take recording, Paul rigged a system to layer parts, then built the solid-body electric guitar to reduce feedback.
facts: He recorded harmonies with himself years before studios could
Manufacturers initially rejected his guitar design

06-10.title: 'Ain't No Half Steppin' announced Brooklyn's technical peak
06-10.story: Big Daddy Kane's Bed-Stuy delivery combined speed, clarity and swing, setting a standard other rappers openly chased.
facts: He wrote for Biz Markie and Roxanne Shanté as well
His breath control is still studied by MCs

06-11.title: Which 'Superstar' wins: Delaney & Bonnie or the Carpenters?
06-11.story: Originally a rough rock lament, the Carpenters' 1971 arrangement turned it into a lush, aching ballad with an oboe line.
facts: Richard Carpenter reworked the harmony substantially
Karen Carpenter sang the vocal from a rough scratch take that was kept

06-12.title: Nile Rodgers wrote 'Le Freak' after being turned away
06-12.story: Refused entry to Studio 54, Rodgers and Edwards went home angry and wrote a chorus built on an expletive, later changed to 'freak out'.
facts: The original hook was considerably ruder
It became Atlantic Records' biggest-selling single

06-13.title: Tape delay was invented using two machines
06-13.story: Engineers fed a signal from one tape head to another, creating slapback echo. Sun Studio's version defined early rock and roll vocals.
facts: Elvis's voice at Sun is drenched in it
The delay time depended on physical head spacing

06-14.title: 'The Message' proved rap could report the news
06-14.story: Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five released a bleak social document at a time when rap was expected to be party music.
facts: Most of the group disliked the song initially
Melle Mel delivers nearly all of it

06-15.title: Ditmas Park's block parties keep the sound-system tradition
06-15.story: Summer street closures along Cortelyou and Rugby Road turned into speaker-stack parties, echoing Caribbean sound-system culture nearby.
facts: Permits are typically pulled by block associations
DJs still run generators for outdoor sets

06-16.title: Tupac studied ballet and Shakespeare
06-16.story: Shakur trained at the Baltimore School for the Arts, performing in ballet and theatre before rapping professionally.
facts: He played the Mouse King in The Nutcracker
He credited acting training for his delivery

06-17.title: The Linn drum machine used real recorded drums
06-17.story: Roger Linn sampled actual drum hits instead of synthesizing them, giving eighties pop its crisp, oversized snare.
facts: Prince built much of his sound on the LM-1
It cost roughly as much as a car

06-18.title: Paul McCartney woke up with 'Yesterday' in his head
06-18.story: McCartney dreamed the melody and spent weeks asking people if he had accidentally stolen it. Placeholder lyrics were 'scrambled eggs'.
facts: It is among the most covered songs ever written
He recorded it alone with a string quartet

06-19.title: Juneteenth and the blues' long road north
06-19.story: Emancipation's spread carried musical traditions from the Deep South up through Memphis and Chicago, reshaping American popular music.
facts: The Great Migration moved the blues to electric amplification
Chicago's louder clubs demanded volume country blues never needed

06-20.title: Brian Wilson built 'Pet Sounds' while the band toured
06-20.story: Wilson stopped touring and recorded the album with session players, presenting finished tracks to the Beach Boys on their return.
facts: He used bicycle bells, dog whistles and empty bottles
Some bandmates initially resisted the material

06-21.title: 'Funky Worm' gave G-funk its whine
06-21.story: The Ohio Players' high synthesizer squeal became the signature lead sound of West Coast hip-hop two decades later.
facts: Dr. Dre used the tone repeatedly
The original was meant as a comic effect

06-22.title: Which 'Valerie' wins: The Zutons or Amy Winehouse?
06-22.story: The Zutons wrote it as indie rock. Mark Ronson and Amy Winehouse recut it as sixties soul, and that version eclipsed the original.
facts: Ronson built the arrangement around a Motown-style backbeat
Winehouse recorded her vocal quickly, largely live

06-23.title: Bessie Smith outsold nearly every artist of her era
06-23.story: Smith's records sold in the hundreds of thousands to Black audiences largely ignored by the mainstream industry.
facts: She toured in her own railroad car
Her success proved a market executives had denied existed

06-24.title: The Neve console became a producer's instrument
06-24.story: Rupert Neve's circuitry added a warmth engineers still chase. Studios built entire reputations on owning one.
facts: Plugins now emulate specific serial numbers
Neve designed to a spec, not a sound, and got both

06-25.title: Michael Jackson died, and streaming spiked worldwide
06-25.story: Jackson's death caused traffic surges that briefly destabilized major websites, an early sign of how music news moved online.
facts: Some services mistook the traffic for an attack
'Thriller' remains the best-selling album ever

06-26.title: Sly Stone assembled America's first fully integrated band
06-26.story: Sly and the Family Stone included Black and white members, men and women, all sharing lead vocals, unprecedented at the time.
facts: Trumpeter Cynthia Robinson was a rare female horn lead
The lineup was itself a political statement

06-27.title: 'Nautilus' became crate-diggers' holy grail
06-27.story: Bob James's track hid a haunting synth figure that producers mined for decades, often unaware others had found it too.
facts: It anchors multiple hip-hop classics
James has said he is delighted by its second life

06-28.title: Gil Scott-Heron read poetry over congas
06-28.story: 'The Revolution Will Not Be Televised' was spoken word over percussion, an ancestor of rap that Scott-Heron resisted being called.
facts: He preferred the term 'bluesologist'
The first version used only congas and voice

06-29.title: Little Richard's 'Tutti Frutti' had to be rewritten on the spot
06-29.story: The original lyrics were far too explicit for radio, so a local songwriter rewrote them during a lunch break at the session.
facts: The rewrite took roughly 15 minutes
Richard's piano intro was kept exactly as first played

06-30.title: Brooklyn's Celebrate Brooklyn keeps free music alive
06-30.story: The Prospect Park bandshell series has run for over four decades, one of the last major free festivals in New York.
facts: It draws crowds from across Flatbush and Ditmas Park
Many artists play it before headlining paid venues

07-01.title: Stravinsky's premiere caused a riot
07-01.story: 'The Rite of Spring' provoked shouting and fistfights at its Paris debut. The dancers could not hear the orchestra over the noise.
facts: The choreographer shouted counts from the wings
It is now standard repertoire worldwide

07-02.title: Which 'Hallelujah' wins: Cohen or Buckley?
07-02.story: Leonard Cohen wrote around 80 verses and released a restrained gospel-tinged version. Jeff Buckley's 1994 reading, learned from John Cale's cover, made it a standard.
facts: Cohen spent years writing it, reportedly banging his head on a hotel floor
Buckley's take is a single guitar and voice, recorded largely live

07-03.title: Bernie Worrell made the synthesizer funky
07-03.story: Parliament-Funkadelic's keyboardist treated the Moog as a bass instrument, inventing the squelching low end that shaped G-funk two decades later.
facts: He was classically trained and wrote a concerto as a child
Dr. Dre's nineties productions lean directly on his vocabulary

07-04.title: Which 'Girls Just Want to Have Fun' wins: Hazard or Lauper?
07-04.story: Robert Hazard wrote it from a man's perspective as a demo. Cyndi Lauper rewrote the meaning entirely, turning it into a feminist anthem.
facts: Lauper initially disliked the song and refused to record it
She rewrote lyrics to flip the point of view

07-05.title: The Ditmas Park porch concert circuit
07-05.story: Neighbors around Cortelyou Road turned Victorian porches into micro-venues, hosting acoustic sets for audiences of thirty. The tradition continues each summer.
facts: Some porches host annual multi-act bills
The format traces back to house-party culture across Flatbush

07-06.title: Coney Island's boardwalk had its own sound
07-06.story: Amusement park organs, barkers and competing radios created a dense collage that New York songwriters mined for decades. The Tilyou family's Steeplechase organ was audible for blocks.
facts: Band organs were built to cut through crowd noise without amplification
Brighton Beach's Russian clubs later added a second musical layer nearby

07-07.title: The 'Loud War' shrank music's dynamic range
07-07.story: Mastering engineers began compressing records to sound louder than competitors on radio and CD changers. The side effect was flattened peaks and listening fatigue.
facts: Some nineties reissues are quieter than their originals by design
Streaming loudness normalization has since reduced the incentive

07-08.title: Nina Simone played Carnegie Hall, but not as she planned
07-08.story: When Simone finally reached Carnegie Hall, she noted bitterly that she arrived as a pop singer, not the classical concert pianist she trained to be.
facts: She opened sets with Bach preludes to make the point
Her civil-rights songs cost her radio play and income

07-09.title: Leap day gave Gioachino Rossini a rare birthday
07-09.story: Born on 29 February, Rossini joked he only aged once every four years. He retired from opera at 37 and spent decades writing small pieces and cooking.
facts: He wrote 'The Barber of Seville' in about three weeks
He named several compositions after food

07-10.title: Elvis recorded his first single for his mother
07-10.story: At 18, Presley paid Sun Studio's $4 fee to cut 'My Happiness' as a gift. Receptionist Marion Keisker secretly taped a copy because she liked his voice.
facts: Her note read: 'Good ballad singer. Hold.'
That saved tape led Sam Phillips to call him back a year later

07-11.title: Dolly Parton wrote two standards on the same day
07-11.story: Parton has said she wrote 'Jolene' and 'I Will Always Love You' in a single writing session. One was about a bank teller flirting with her husband; the other about leaving her mentor.
facts: Elvis wanted to record 'I Will Always Love You' but his manager demanded publishing
She said no, and kept the rights that later made her a fortune

07-12.title: The Clash recorded 'London Calling' with a producer who threw chairs
07-12.story: Guy Stevens motivated takes by swinging ladders and pouring wine on the piano. The chaos was intentional; he wanted performances, not perfection.
facts: Engineer Bill Price quietly kept the tape rolling through the mayhem
The title track's bass was played by Paul Simonon, who learned bass in the band

07-13.title: Marilyn Monroe's birthday and the art of the breathy mic
07-13.story: Close-mic crooning only became possible with sensitive condenser microphones, letting singers whisper instead of project.
facts: Before electric mics, singers needed opera-level volume
The intimate vocal style is a technology story as much as a taste one

07-14.title: Les Paul invented multitrack recording in his garage
07-14.story: Frustrated by one-take recording, Paul rigged a system to layer parts, then built the solid-body electric guitar to reduce feedback.
facts: He recorded harmonies with himself years before studios could
Manufacturers initially rejected his guitar design

07-15.title: The Linn drum machine used real recorded drums
07-15.story: Roger Linn sampled actual drum hits instead of synthesizing them, giving eighties pop its crisp, oversized snare.
facts: Prince built much of his sound on the LM-1
It cost roughly as much as a car

07-16.title: Michael Jackson died, and streaming spiked worldwide
07-16.story: Jackson's death caused traffic surges that briefly destabilized major websites, an early sign of how music news moved online.
facts: Some services mistook the traffic for an attack
'Thriller' remains the best-selling album ever

07-17.title: 'The Star-Spangled Banner' was set to a drinking song
07-17.story: Francis Scott Key's poem was matched to 'To Anacreon in Heaven', a British social club tune notorious for its difficult octave-and-a-half range.
facts: That range is why singers so often struggle with it
It became the official anthem only in 1931

07-18.title: Bobby McFerrin used no instruments at all
07-18.story: 'Don't Worry, Be Happy' is entirely voice and body percussion, multitracked. Listeners assumed they were hearing a full band.
facts: Every sound including the bass is McFerrin's own voice
It was the first a cappella song to top the US chart

07-19.title: Wagner built a theater to control how his music was heard
07-19.story: Frustrated by noisy houses, Wagner designed Bayreuth with a hidden orchestra pit and a darkened hall, inventing conventions concert audiences still follow.
facts: Darkening the auditorium was considered radical
The sunken pit blends the orchestra into a single sound

07-20.title: Mariah Carey co-wrote nearly everything she sang
07-20.story: Unusual for a young pop signing, Carey held writing credits from her debut, giving her long-term control of her catalogue.
facts: She uses the whistle register, a rare vocal extreme
Her demo reached a label head at a party by chance

07-21.title: 'Sing Sing' delivered the drums for a hip-hop decade
07-21.story: Gaz's 'Sing Sing' and its cousins supplied breaks that New York DJs guarded like secrets, soaking labels off records to hide titles.
facts: DJs soaked or scratched off labels to protect their sources
Digging culture grew directly from that secrecy

07-22.title: The Winstons' break has its own documentary
07-22.story: Decades after 'Amen, Brother', filmmakers traced how six seconds spawned entire scenes without the band's knowledge or payment.
facts: Copyright never protected the drummer's performance itself
Public fundraising eventually delivered some belated compensation

07-23.title: Bach's music was rescued by a butcher's wrapping paper
07-23.story: Legend holds Mendelssohn found Bach manuscripts used as packing material, sparking the revival that restored Bach to the canon.
facts: He staged the St Matthew Passion after 100 years of neglect
Bach was known mainly as an organist in his lifetime

07-24.title: Gladys Knight had the first 'Grapevine' hit, then lost it
07-24.story: Gladys Knight and the Pips charted with 'I Heard It Through the Grapevine' before Marvin Gaye's slower version eclipsed it entirely.
facts: Motown shelved Gaye's take for over a year
Gaye's version became the label's biggest-selling single to that point

07-25.title: The Amen break is six seconds long and built three genres
07-25.story: Chopped and sped up, the Winstons' break became the engine of jungle, drum and bass and UK hardcore, often at double its original tempo.
facts: Producers slice it into individual hits and rebuild new patterns
A crowdfunding campaign later raised money for the surviving band member

hits: Oasis - D'You Know What I Mean?

07-26.title: Carole King wrote hits in Brooklyn before singing them
07-26.story: Born in Manhattan and raised in Brooklyn, King wrote dozens of standards with Gerry Goffin before 'Tapestry' made her a performer.
facts: She attended James Madison High School in Brooklyn
'Will You Love Me Tomorrow' was written when she was 17

07-27.title: Prince died, leaving a vault of unreleased music
07-27.story: Prince recorded relentlessly, storing thousands of unreleased tracks in a bank-style vault at Paisley Park. Estimates suggest decades of material.
facts: He often recorded alone overnight, engineering himself
Some vault songs date to the seventies

07-28.title: Duke Ellington wrote for specific players, not instruments
07-28.story: Ellington composed around individual musicians' quirks, writing parts only they could play. Replacing a member meant rewriting the music.
facts: He called his orchestra his real instrument
He wrote on trains between gigs for decades

07-29.title: The Beastie Boys started as a Brooklyn hardcore band
07-29.story: Before rapping, the Beastie Boys played fast hardcore punk around New York. Their pivot to hip-hop began as a joke track that got better reactions than their punk set.
facts: Their first release was a hardcore EP, not a rap record
They kept playing instruments themselves long after going platinum

07-30.title: Handel wrote 'Messiah' in 24 days
07-30.story: Working almost without sleep, Handel completed the 259-page score in just over three weeks. A servant reported finding him weeping at his desk.
facts: It premiered in Dublin, not London
Audiences were asked to leave hoops and swords at home to fit more people in

07-31.title: Kurt Cobain was born, and later hid melodies in noise
07-31.story: Cobain's writing method paired sweet pop melody with deliberately abrasive tone, a tension he credited to loving both the Beatles and Black Flag.
facts: 'Nevermind' was mixed to sound more polished than the band wanted
He wrote lyrics minutes before recording many vocals

08-01.title: The Moog synthesizer needed a hit to be taken seriously
08-01.story: Wendy Carlos's 'Switched-On Bach' proved the Moog could make music, not just noise. It became one of the best-selling classical records ever.
facts: Each note had to be played and layered one at a time
The instrument was monophonic, so chords required many passes

08-02.title: The piano on 'Layla' was never meant to be there
08-02.story: Drummer Jim Gordon was caught playing a private piano melody during downtime. Eric Clapton heard it through the studio glass and insisted it become the song's second half.
facts: The coda was recorded months after the main track
The two halves were spliced together with tape, not re-performed

08-03.title: Stevie Wonder played nearly every instrument on 'Innervisions'
08-03.story: Wonder recorded drums, keys, bass and harmonica himself, layering parts alone in the studio through the night. Engineers worked in shifts to keep up with him.
facts: He often worked 48-hour sessions without leaving
The clavinet sound on 'Higher Ground' was cut in about three hours

08-04.title: Nina Simone trained as a classical pianist, not a singer
08-04.story: Denied a place at the Curtis Institute, Simone took a bar job that required singing. She had only ever intended to play Bach, and that classical phrasing never left her.
facts: Her improvisations often quote Bach fugues mid-song
She sang publicly for the first time only because the club owner insisted

08-05.title: Why reggae's bass sits so far forward
08-05.story: Jamaican records were made for outdoor sound systems where bass carried across a street. Engineers cut low frequencies hot and pulled the treble back.
facts: Producers tested mixes on actual street speakers before release
This is the root of dub, born from stripping vocals off those mixes

08-06.title: Brooklyn's Kings Theatre reopening drew a Flatbush crowd
08-06.story: After decades dark, the Flatbush palace reopened with a sold-out show, restoring a major venue to the neighborhood's doorstep.
facts: Restoration took roughly four years
It is among the largest theaters in Brooklyn

08-07.title: Tupac studied ballet and Shakespeare
08-07.story: Shakur trained at the Baltimore School for the Arts, performing in ballet and theatre before rapping professionally.
facts: He played the Mouse King in The Nutcracker
He credited acting training for his delivery

08-08.title: The Neve console became a producer's instrument
08-08.story: Rupert Neve's circuitry added a warmth engineers still chase. Studios built entire reputations on owning one.
facts: Plugins now emulate specific serial numbers
Neve designed to a spec, not a sound, and got both

08-09.title: Lou Reed recorded an album designed to be unlistenable
08-09.story: 'Metal Machine Music' was 64 minutes of guitar feedback. Reed said it was sincere; the label suspected he was escaping a contract.
facts: It was returned by buyers in enormous numbers
Decades later, an ensemble performed it as scored contemporary music

08-10.title: The first commercial radio broadcast changed listening forever
08-10.story: Early stations discovered that recorded music filled airtime cheaply. Within a decade, radio play, not sheet music, determined what became a hit.
facts: Sheet music sales collapsed as radio grew
Record labels initially fought radio, fearing it would kill sales

08-11.title: John Coltrane practiced until his lips bled
08-11.story: Bandmates described Coltrane practicing 12 hours a day, sometimes falling asleep with the horn in his mouth. 'Giant Steps' came from that obsession.
facts: Its chord changes are still a rite of passage for jazz students
Pianist Tommy Flanagan sight-read the session and struggled famously

08-12.title: Pink Floyd recorded a heartbeat to open an album
08-12.story: 'The Dark Side of the Moon' opens with a treated bass drum simulating a pulse, then loops of interviews with studio staff answering existential questions.
facts: Paul McCartney was interviewed but his answers were unused
The album charted for over 900 weeks

08-13.title: James Jamerson never wrote his basslines down
08-13.story: Motown's uncredited bassist improvised most parts on first take. Because nothing was notated, many lines were lost when he died.
facts: He appears on more number ones than the Beatles and Elvis combined
He was not credited on album sleeves for most of his career

08-14.title: Bob Marley survived being shot and played two days later
08-14.story: Gunmen wounded Marley at his Kingston home before a peace concert. He performed anyway, showing the crowd his injured arm.
facts: He said 'the people who are trying to make this world worse aren't taking a day off'
He left Jamaica for London shortly after

08-15.title: 'Impeach the President' gave hip-hop its snare
08-15.story: The Honey Drippers' record, cut by a high-school band, contains a drum intro that became a foundation of nineties New York production.
facts: Its snare defines much of the boom-bap era
The players were teenagers when they recorded it

extra.src: The Honey Drippers - Impeach the President (1973)
hits: Janet Jackson - That's the Way Love Goes

08-16.title: Brooklyn's Fulton Street record shops fed the DJs
08-16.story: Independent shops along Fulton and Flatbush stocked breaks, imports and white labels that defined what Brooklyn DJs could play.
facts: Shop owners often acted as informal A&R
Many crews formed in the aisles

08-17.title: Marvin Gaye's 'Inner City Blues' hid a second bassline
08-17.story: Bassist Bob Babbitt and James Jamerson both appear across the album, and Gaye layered a second bass an octave apart to thicken the low end.
facts: Jamerson famously recorded lying flat on his back
He played most parts with a single index finger, nicknamed 'The Hook'

08-18.title: The 'Think' break gave hip-hop its whistle
08-18.story: Lyn Collins' 'Think (About It)', produced by James Brown, supplied the 'woo! yeah!' stabs heard on hundreds of records.
facts: Rob Base and DJ E-Z Rock built an entire hit on it
The vocal stabs are now shorthand for party records

08-19.title: Luther Vandross sang jingles before he sang ballads
08-19.story: Vandross earned a living singing commercials and backing vocals for Bowie and Chic before launching a solo career.
facts: He arranged the backing vocals on Bowie's 'Young Americans'
He sang on ads for soft drinks and fast food chains

08-20.title: Ann Peebles wrote a hit about wanting bad weather
08-20.story: 'I Can't Stand the Rain' came from an offhand complaint about going out in a storm. Her co-writers turned the line into the hook on the spot.
facts: John Lennon called it the best song he'd ever heard
The opening electric timbale imitates falling rain

08-21.title: Biggie recorded his debut while still selling on the corner
08-21.story: 'Ready to Die' was cut while Christopher Wallace was living on St. James Place in Clinton Hill. Producers have described him writing nothing down, holding entire verses in his head.
facts: He never used a pen in the booth, a habit Jay-Z also adopted
The album's skits map his actual Brooklyn upbringing

08-22.title: Whitney Houston's mother sang backup for Aretha
08-22.story: Cissy Houston led the Sweet Inspirations, who sang behind Aretha Franklin and Elvis. Whitney grew up in studios watching that work.
facts: Dionne Warwick is her cousin
