Cissy also sang on Van Morrison's 'Brown Eyed Girl' sessions era material

08-23.title: Smokey Robinson wrote the song Motown almost rejected
08-23.story: 'The Tracks of My Tears' came from a guitar figure Marv Tarplin played for weeks before lyrics existed. Robinson wrote to the guitar, not the other way around.
facts: Bob Dylan reportedly called Robinson America's greatest living poet
The guitar intro was kept exactly as Tarplin first improvised it

08-24.title: Brooklyn's Prospect Park bandshell started a free summer tradition
08-24.story: Celebrate Brooklyn began as a modest neighborhood series and grew into one of America's longest-running free outdoor festivals, minutes from Ditmas Park.
facts: It launched partly to bring people back into the park after a rough decade
Acts range from Afrobeat legends to local Brooklyn bands

08-25.title: Kraftwerk built their own instruments because none existed
08-25.story: For 'Autobahn', the band constructed custom electronic drums and vocoders in their Kling Klang studio. They were chasing the sound of a car trip, not a band.
facts: The whooshing traffic sounds are synthesized, not recorded
The 22-minute original was cut to three minutes for radio and became a global hit

08-26.title: The Roland TR-808 flopped before it changed everything
08-26.story: Roland discontinued the drum machine after three years because it sounded fake next to real drums. Producers bought them cheap secondhand, and its booming kick became the spine of hip-hop.
facts: The 808's sound came from faulty transistors Roland bought as a batch
When that supply ran out, the machine could not be made again

08-27.title: Why 'Bohemian Rhapsody' took three weeks of overdubs
08-27.story: Queen layered their vocal harmonies up to 180 times, bouncing tape so often it wore thin. Held to the light, the master was nearly transparent.
facts: The band sang 10-12 hours a day for the opera section
No synthesizers were used; the album sleeve said so proudly

08-28.title: The Beatles' last live show was on a roof
08-28.story: With no venue and no plan, the band played atop their Savile Row office. London police shut it down after 42 minutes, which is why the film has an ending.
facts: Office workers watched from surrounding rooftops
It was the final time all four performed publicly together

08-29.title: Prince changed his name to a symbol to escape a contract
08-29.story: In a dispute with Warner Bros., Prince adopted an unpronounceable glyph and wrote 'slave' on his face at appearances.
facts: Media resorted to calling him 'the artist formerly known as'
Floppy disks with the symbol font were mailed to press

08-30.title: Ditmas Park's block parties keep the sound-system tradition
08-30.story: Summer street closures along Cortelyou and Rugby Road turned into speaker-stack parties, echoing Caribbean sound-system culture nearby.
facts: Permits are typically pulled by block associations
DJs still run generators for outdoor sets

08-31.title: Bessie Smith outsold nearly every artist of her era
08-31.story: Smith's records sold in the hundreds of thousands to Black audiences largely ignored by the mainstream industry.
facts: She toured in her own railroad car
Her success proved a market executives had denied existed

09-01.title: Chopin and the piano that never left the room
09-01.story: Chopin wrote almost exclusively for solo piano, rarely performing in large halls because his playing was too quiet. He preferred salons of a few dozen listeners.
facts: He gave roughly 30 public concerts in his entire life
His pupils described his rubato as 'the tree keeps time, the leaves sway'

09-02.title: Ella Fitzgerald invented her scat by copying horns
09-02.story: Fitzgerald built solos by imitating trumpet and saxophone lines rather than singing words, turning her voice into a brass instrument.
facts: She could reproduce bebop solos note for note
Her 'Songbook' series helped canonize American standards

09-03.title: Nas recorded 'Illmatic' with four different producers
09-03.story: Rather than one house sound, Nas invited DJ Premier, Pete Rock, Q-Tip and Large Professor. The album runs under 40 minutes with no filler.
facts: He was 20 when it was released
Its brevity was deliberate; he cut anything that repeated an idea

09-04.title: Aretha Franklin was born, and learned in her father's church
09-04.story: Franklin grew up singing gospel in Detroit under her preacher father, absorbing a call-and-response phrasing she never abandoned in secular music.
facts: She played piano on many of her own recordings
Her Atlantic breakthrough came after Columbia tried to make her a pop crooner

09-05.title: Which 'Blinded by the Light' wins: Springsteen or Manfred Mann?
09-05.story: Springsteen's original is a wordy folk-rock rush. Manfred Mann's Earth Band slowed it, changed a lyric and scored the only Springsteen-written US number one.
facts: Springsteen has joked he never had a chart-topper with his own version
The famous misheard lyric comes from Mann's rewrite

09-06.title: Bo Hansson and the rise of the bedroom studio
09-06.story: Long before home recording was normal, musicians began assembling private studios, shifting power away from label-owned rooms.
facts: Multitrack tape became affordable in the seventies
This lineage runs directly to laptop production today

09-07.title: Delia Derbyshire realized the Doctor Who theme with tape
09-07.story: Working without synthesizers, Derbyshire built the theme by recording single tones, cutting the tape and splicing pitches by hand.
facts: Each note was measured with a ruler
She received no on-screen composer credit for years

09-08.title: Which 'Killing Me Softly' wins: Flack or the Fugees?
09-08.story: Roberta Flack's version is intimate and slow. The Fugees rebuilt it in 1996 over a hip-hop break with Lauryn Hill's lead.
facts: Flack publicly praised the remake
The Fugees kept the melody almost unchanged

09-09.title: Nile Rodgers' guitar is on more hits than you think
09-09.story: The Chic guitarist's clipped 'chucking' style powered his own band, then Bowie's 'Let's Dance', Madonna's 'Like a Virgin' and Daft Punk's 'Get Lucky'.
facts: He uses a 1960 Stratocaster he calls 'The Hitmaker'
He and Bernard Edwards wrote Sister Sledge's catalogue too

09-10.title: Which 'I Will Always Love You' wins: Dolly or Whitney?
09-10.story: Dolly Parton wrote it as a quiet goodbye to her mentor. Whitney Houston's 1992 version added the a cappella opening that producer David Foster fought for.
facts: Parton has said she cried hearing Whitney's version on the radio
The a cappella intro was nearly cut for being too risky

09-11.title: 'Apache' is called the national anthem of hip-hop
09-11.story: The Incredible Bongo Band's cover gave DJs a long percussion break perfect for cutting between two turntables.
facts: Kool Herc played it at Bronx block parties
The break is essentially a drum solo with congas

hits: LL Cool J - You Can't Dance

09-12.title: 'Change the Beat' gave the world its most-scratched sound
09-12.story: The 'ahhh, fresh' vocoder phrase at the end of Fab 5 Freddy's record became the single most-scratched sample in DJ history.
facts: It was recorded almost as an afterthought at the session's end
Nearly every turntablist routine still uses it

09-13.title: The Kings Theatre sat dark for 36 years
09-13.story: The Flatbush Avenue movie palace closed in 1977 and decayed with trees growing through the roof. A restoration reopened it in 2015 as one of Brooklyn's great music rooms.
facts: Original 1929 plasterwork was recast from surviving fragments
It now seats roughly 3,000 for concerts a mile from Ditmas Park

09-14.title: Dub was born by accident when a vocal track was left off
09-14.story: Engineer King Tubby pressed a version of a record with the vocals missing. Dancers loved it, so he began deliberately stripping tracks and drenching them in echo.
facts: He rewired mixing desks by hand to create his effects
Dub's remix logic is the direct ancestor of electronic dance music

09-15.title: Yoko Ono and John Lennon recorded a heartbeat
09-15.story: Their experimental albums included a recording of their unborn child's heartbeat, followed by silence after the pregnancy was lost. Few records have been that raw.
facts: Critics dismissed the work at the time
It anticipated decades of sound-art practice

09-16.title: Fats Domino sold more records than anyone but Elvis
09-16.story: The New Orleans pianist's rolling triplets defined early rock piano. He recorded almost everything at Cosimo Matassa's tiny J&M studio.
facts: The studio was in the back of an appliance shop
Its cramped room created the signature slapback sound

09-17.title: The bassline Paul McCartney built from a mistake
09-17.story: On 'Paperback Writer', McCartney wanted a bass so loud it would rattle radios. Engineer Ken Townsend rigged a loudspeaker as a microphone to capture the low end, a trick no one had tried.
facts: EMI's rulebook technically forbade the setup
The result was the loudest bass ever pressed to a Beatles single to that point

09-18.title: Brian Eno wrote rules on cards to break writer's block
09-18.story: Frustrated in the studio, Eno printed 'Oblique Strategies' — cards with instructions like 'Honour thy error as a hidden intention'. Musicians drew one when stuck.
facts: Bowie used the deck heavily during the Berlin albums
One card simply reads 'Do nothing for as long as possible'

09-19.title: The Fairlight sampler cost as much as a house
09-19.story: The first commercial digital sampler sold for tens of thousands of dollars, limiting it to stars like Kate Bush and Peter Gabriel. It let musicians play any recorded sound from a keyboard.
facts: Bush used it to turn breaking glass into an instrument
Its low memory forced the short, clipped samples that define the era

09-20.title: Talking Heads built 'Remain in Light' from loops before loops existed
09-20.story: The band recorded single-bar grooves and spliced them into endless cycles by hand with razor blades and tape, inspired by Fela Kuti's Afrobeat.
facts: Each member recorded parts separately, never playing the song together
Eno and Byrne assembled the arrangements afterward

09-21.title: Prince Buster shaped the beat that became ska
09-21.story: Buster instructed guitarists to accent the offbeat, flipping Jamaican R&B into ska and eventually rocksteady and reggae.
facts: He staged sound-system clashes as public theatre
Two-tone bands in Britain rebuilt his catalogue

09-22.title: 'The Message' proved rap could report the news
09-22.story: Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five released a bleak social document at a time when rap was expected to be party music.
facts: Most of the group disliked the song initially
Melle Mel delivers nearly all of it

09-23.title: Which 'Valerie' wins: The Zutons or Amy Winehouse?
09-23.story: The Zutons wrote it as indie rock. Mark Ronson and Amy Winehouse recut it as sixties soul, and that version eclipsed the original.
facts: Ronson built the arrangement around a Motown-style backbeat
Winehouse recorded her vocal quickly, largely live

09-24.title: Brooklyn's Celebrate Brooklyn keeps free music alive
09-24.story: The Prospect Park bandshell series has run for over four decades, one of the last major free festivals in New York.
facts: It draws crowds from across Flatbush and Ditmas Park
Many artists play it before headlining paid venues

09-25.title: Jay-Z grew up in Marcy Houses
09-25.story: Shawn Carter's Bed-Stuy childhood is stitched through his catalogue. Like Biggie, he famously records without writing lyrics down.
facts: He founded Roc-A-Fella after labels passed on signing him
Marcy Houses appears by name across three decades of his songs

09-26.title: The Ramones played 2:30 songs to fit more into a set
09-26.story: Their debut cost about $6,400 and ran under 30 minutes. Speed and brevity were economic decisions as much as aesthetic ones.
facts: They counted off every song identically
The whole album was recorded in about a week

09-27.title: The Wrecking Crew played on records credited to bands
09-27.story: A pool of Los Angeles session musicians performed on hits attributed to famous groups. Many listeners never knew.
facts: Carol Kaye played bass on hundreds of well-known records
Some bands only learned their own parts after release

09-28.title: 'Sunshine of Your Love' came from a bass riff heard at a gig
09-28.story: Jack Bruce wrote the riff after seeing Jimi Hendrix play live and going home to his bass at dawn.
facts: Ginger Baker's tom pattern was inspired by Native American rhythms
The band nearly rejected it as too simple

09-29.title: Which 'Nothing Compares 2 U' wins: Prince or Sinéad?
09-29.story: Prince wrote it for his side project The Family. Sinéad O'Connor's 1990 version, with its single-shot video, became definitive.
facts: Her tears in the video were reportedly unplanned
Prince rarely performed it before her version succeeded

09-30.title: Bill Withers was making toilet seats for airplanes
09-30.story: Withers kept his factory job while recording 'Ain't No Sunshine', assuming music would not last. The famous repeated 'I know' was a placeholder.
facts: He meant to write real lyrics there but was told to keep it
He brought his lunchbox to the studio

10-01.title: Miles Davis plugged in and lost half his audience
10-01.story: 'Bitches Brew' used electric instruments and studio editing, alienating purists while inventing fusion.
facts: Producer Teo Macero spliced the tapes like a film editor
Long passages were assembled, not performed continuously

10-02.title: Which 'Respect' wins: Otis or Aretha?
10-02.story: Otis Redding wrote it in 1965 as a working man's plea. Aretha Franklin rebuilt it in 1967 as a demand, adding the spelling hook and her sisters' backing vocals.
facts: Redding joked she had stolen the song for good
Aretha's version was cut in a single afternoon session

10-03.title: 'Under Pressure' was a jam nobody planned
10-03.story: Bowie and Queen were in the same Swiss studio and started improvising. The famous bassline came from John Deacon noodling during a break.
facts: Accounts differ on who actually invented the riff
Vanilla Ice later used it and initially denied the resemblance

10-04.title: The producer who never let artists hear playback
10-04.story: Phil Spector often refused to let performers hear the full mix, keeping the arrangement in his head so no one could argue with it.
facts: Sessions ran for hours with dozens of players
Darlene Love's voice appeared on records credited to other groups

10-05.title: Grandmaster Flash built his mixer by hand
10-05.story: Trained in electronics, Flash rigged a crossfader and cue system so he could hear the next record before the crowd did.
facts: He soldered parts salvaged from junked stereos
That preview capability made beat-matching possible

10-06.title: Erasmus Hall in Flatbush produced two American icons
10-06.story: Barbra Streisand and Neil Diamond both sang in the chorus at Erasmus Hall High School on Flatbush Avenue, a short walk from Cortelyou Road. They barely knew each other then.
facts: They later recorded the duet 'You Don't Bring Me Flowers' in 1978
Clive Davis, who signed Springsteen and Whitney Houston, also went to Erasmus

10-07.title: The Beatles played Ed Sullivan to 73 million people
10-07.story: Broadcast from CBS Studio 50 in Manhattan, the performance was watched by roughly 40 percent of America. Crime rates that hour reportedly dipped.
facts: The studio received 50,000 ticket requests for 700 seats
Sullivan had booked them after seeing fan chaos at Heathrow

10-08.title: Autotune was invented by an oil industry engineer
10-08.story: Andy Hildebrand used seismic data math, designed to find oil underground, to detect and correct pitch. He built it as a subtle repair tool.
facts: Cher's 'Believe' used the extreme setting the inventor called a joke
Hildebrand said he never expected anyone to use it that way

10-09.title: George Harrison's sitar lesson changed rock
10-09.story: Harrison studied under Ravi Shankar, who insisted he learn properly rather than use the instrument as decoration. Indian modes then filtered into Western pop.
facts: Shankar initially had no idea who the Beatles were
'Within You Without You' features no other Beatle

10-10.title: Why Motown mixed its records on a car speaker
10-10.story: Berry Gordy kept a cheap car-dashboard speaker wired into the Hitsville control room. If a mix didn't hit on that tinny cone, it went back, because that's where America actually heard music.
facts: Engineers called the test 'the Detroit ear'
Motown also boosted mid-range so songs cut through AM radio static

10-11.title: Why disco records used real strings and a metronome
10-11.story: Philadelphia producers paired full orchestras with a rigid four-on-the-floor kick so DJs could beat-match by hand. The click track was the secret that made mixing possible.
facts: Engineers printed the tempo on the record label for DJs
This is why so many disco 12-inches sit near 120 beats per minute

10-12.title: Prince played 27 instruments on his debut
10-12.story: Warner Bros. doubted a 19-year-old could produce himself, so Prince recorded a demo playing every part. He got full creative control, almost unheard of for a new artist.
facts: He reportedly recorded the album in about five weeks
His contract made him one of the youngest self-producing artists on a major label

10-13.title: Robert Johnson recorded facing the corner of a room
10-13.story: In a San Antonio hotel room, Johnson played into the corner. For years it was called superstition; engineers now note it created natural bass reinforcement.
facts: Only 29 songs of his survive
The corner technique is a real acoustic trick still used today

10-14.title: Bill Withers recorded 'Grandma's Hands' in under two minutes
10-14.story: Withers wrote about his grandmother's church in West Virginia. The song is barely 120 seconds long and needed nothing more.
facts: Blackstreet later built 'No Diggity' on its bones
He resisted adding a bridge, saying it was finished

10-15.title: Tape delay was invented using two machines
10-15.story: Engineers fed a signal from one tape head to another, creating slapback echo. Sun Studio's version defined early rock and roll vocals.
facts: Elvis's voice at Sun is drenched in it
The delay time depended on physical head spacing

10-16.title: 'Funky Worm' gave G-funk its whine
10-16.story: The Ohio Players' high synthesizer squeal became the signature lead sound of West Coast hip-hop two decades later.
facts: Dr. Dre used the tone repeatedly
The original was meant as a comic effect

10-17.title: Little Richard's 'Tutti Frutti' had to be rewritten on the spot
10-17.story: The original lyrics were far too explicit for radio, so a local songwriter rewrote them during a lunch break at the session.
facts: The rewrite took roughly 15 minutes
Richard's piano intro was kept exactly as first played

10-18.title: Maurice Ravel wrote 'Boléro' as an experiment in repetition
10-18.story: Ravel called it 'orchestral tissue without music', a single melody repeated with growing instrumentation and no development. He was surprised it became famous.
facts: The snare drum plays the same rhythm for roughly 15 minutes
He reportedly said the piece contained 'no music in it whatsoever'

10-19.title: Sister Rosetta Tharpe played electric guitar before Chuck Berry
10-19.story: Tharpe's distorted gospel guitar and showmanship directly shaped rock and roll. Berry, Presley and Little Richard all cited her.
facts: She played a solid-body electric in churches, scandalizing congregations
She was inducted into the Rock Hall only in 2018

10-20.title: 'Billie Jean' nearly lost its famous intro
10-20.story: Michael Jackson built the song around a bassline he refused to shorten. Quincy Jones wanted the 29-second intro cut down; Jackson insisted it stay because, in his words, it made him want to dance.
facts: Jackson reportedly recorded the lead vocal through a cardboard tube for tone
The song was mixed roughly 90 times before Jones approved a take

10-21.title: The Wrecking Crew played on records credited to bands
10-21.story: A pool of Los Angeles session musicians performed on hits attributed to famous groups. Many listeners never knew.
facts: Carol Kaye played bass on hundreds of well-known records
Some bands only learned their own parts after release

10-22.title: 'Sunshine of Your Love' came from a bass riff heard at a gig
10-22.story: Jack Bruce wrote the riff after seeing Jimi Hendrix play live and going home to his bass at dawn.
facts: Ginger Baker's tom pattern was inspired by Native American rhythms
The band nearly rejected it as too simple

10-23.title: Which 'Nothing Compares 2 U' wins: Prince or Sinéad?
10-23.story: Prince wrote it for his side project The Family. Sinéad O'Connor's 1990 version, with its single-shot video, became definitive.
facts: Her tears in the video were reportedly unplanned
Prince rarely performed it before her version succeeded

10-24.title: Bill Withers was making toilet seats for airplanes
10-24.story: Withers kept his factory job while recording 'Ain't No Sunshine', assuming music would not last. The famous repeated 'I know' was a placeholder.
facts: He meant to write real lyrics there but was told to keep it
He brought his lunchbox to the studio

10-25.title: Miles Davis plugged in and lost half his audience
10-25.story: 'Bitches Brew' used electric instruments and studio editing, alienating purists while inventing fusion.
facts: Producer Teo Macero spliced the tapes like a film editor
Long passages were assembled, not performed continuously

10-26.title: Which 'Respect' wins: Otis or Aretha?
10-26.story: Otis Redding wrote it in 1965 as a working man's plea. Aretha Franklin rebuilt it in 1967 as a demand, adding the spelling hook and her sisters' backing vocals.
facts: Redding joked she had stolen the song for good
Aretha's version was cut in a single afternoon session

10-27.title: 'Under Pressure' was a jam nobody planned
10-27.story: Bowie and Queen were in the same Swiss studio and started improvising. The famous bassline came from John Deacon noodling during a break.
facts: Accounts differ on who actually invented the riff
Vanilla Ice later used it and initially denied the resemblance

10-28.title: The producer who never let artists hear playback
10-28.story: Phil Spector often refused to let performers hear the full mix, keeping the arrangement in his head so no one could argue with it.
facts: Sessions ran for hours with dozens of players
Darlene Love's voice appeared on records credited to other groups

10-29.title: Grandmaster Flash built his mixer by hand
10-29.story: Trained in electronics, Flash rigged a crossfader and cue system so he could hear the next record before the crowd did.
facts: He soldered parts salvaged from junked stereos
That preview capability made beat-matching possible

10-30.title: Erasmus Hall in Flatbush produced two American icons
10-30.story: Barbra Streisand and Neil Diamond both sang in the chorus at Erasmus Hall High School on Flatbush Avenue, a short walk from Cortelyou Road. They barely knew each other then.
facts: They later recorded the duet 'You Don't Bring Me Flowers' in 1978
Clive Davis, who signed Springsteen and Whitney Houston, also went to Erasmus

11-03.story: Prince cut a rough acoustic demo and handed it to the funk band Mazarati. Producer David Z stripped it to a dry drum machine, chopped the vocals into stabs and added the falsetto arrangement — and when Prince heard it he took the song back.
facts: Mazarati's backing vocals stayed on the finished Prince record
Warner Bros. initially called it too sparse to be a single; it went to number one

11-04.story: On 'Paperback Writer', McCartney wanted a bass so loud it would rattle radios. Engineer Ken Townsend rigged a loudspeaker as a microphone to capture the low end, a trick no one had tried.
facts: EMI's rulebook technically forbade the setup
The result was the loudest bass ever pressed to a Beatles single to that point

11-05.story: Frustrated in the studio, Eno printed 'Oblique Strategies' — cards with instructions like 'Honour thy error as a hidden intention'. Musicians drew one when stuck.
facts: Bowie used the deck heavily during the Berlin albums
One card simply reads 'Do nothing for as long as possible'

11-06.title: 'I Feel Love' was built almost entirely from a Moog
11-06.story: Giorgio Moroder and Pete Bellotte built the backing track for Donna Summer at Munich's Musicland using a Moog modular synthesizer instead of a band. The machine drifted out of tune constantly, so the part was captured in short bursts and edited together.
facts: Engineer Robby Wedel synced the Moog to tape so the sequence could hold time at all
Brian Eno reportedly told Bowie the record would change club music for the next fifteen years

11-07.title: Why 'Bohemian Rhapsody' took three weeks of overdubs
11-07.story: Queen layered their vocal harmonies up to 180 times, bouncing tape so often it wore thin. Held to the light, the master was nearly transparent.
facts: The band sang 10-12 hours a day for the opera section
No synthesizers were used; the album sleeve said so proudly

11-08.title: The Beatles' last live show was on a roof
11-08.story: With no venue and no plan, the band played atop their Savile Row office. London police shut it down after 42 minutes, which is why the film has an ending.
facts: Office workers watched from surrounding rooftops
It was the final time all four performed publicly together

11-09.title: Prince changed his name to a symbol to escape a contract
11-09.story: In a dispute with Warner Bros., Prince adopted an unpronounceable glyph and wrote 'slave' on his face at appearances.
facts: Media resorted to calling him 'the artist formerly known as'
Floppy disks with the symbol font were mailed to press

11-10.title: Ditmas Park's block parties keep the sound-system tradition
11-10.story: Summer street closures along Cortelyou and Rugby Road turned into speaker-stack parties, echoing Caribbean sound-system culture nearby.
facts: Permits are typically pulled by block associations
DJs still run generators for outdoor sets

11-11.title: Bessie Smith outsold nearly every artist of her era
11-11.story: Smith's records sold in the hundreds of thousands to Black audiences largely ignored by the mainstream industry.
facts: She toured in her own railroad car
Her success proved a market executives had denied existed

11-12.title: Chopin and the piano that never left the room
11-12.story: Chopin wrote almost exclusively for solo piano, rarely performing in large halls because his playing was too quiet. He preferred salons of a few dozen listeners.
facts: He gave roughly 30 public concerts in his entire life
His pupils described his rubato as 'the tree keeps time, the leaves sway'

11-13.title: Ella Fitzgerald invented her scat by copying horns
11-13.story: Fitzgerald built solos by imitating trumpet and saxophone lines rather than singing words, turning her voice into a brass instrument.
facts: She could reproduce bebop solos note for note
Her 'Songbook' series helped canonize American standards

11-14.title: Nas recorded 'Illmatic' with four different producers
11-14.story: Rather than one house sound, Nas invited DJ Premier, Pete Rock, Q-Tip and Large Professor. The album runs under 40 minutes with no filler.
facts: He was 20 when it was released
Its brevity was deliberate; he cut anything that repeated an idea

11-15.title: Aretha Franklin was born, and learned in her father's church
11-15.story: Franklin grew up singing gospel in Detroit under her preacher father, absorbing a call-and-response phrasing she never abandoned in secular music.
facts: She played piano on many of her own recordings
Her Atlantic breakthrough came after Columbia tried to make her a pop crooner

11-16.title: Which 'Blinded by the Light' wins: Springsteen or Manfred Mann?
11-16.story: Springsteen's original is a wordy folk-rock rush. Manfred Mann's Earth Band slowed it, changed a lyric and scored the only Springsteen-written US number one.
facts: Springsteen has joked he never had a chart-topper with his own version
The famous misheard lyric comes from Mann's rewrite

11-17.title: Bo Hansson and the rise of the bedroom studio
11-17.story: Long before home recording was normal, musicians began assembling private studios, shifting power away from label-owned rooms.
facts: Multitrack tape became affordable in the seventies
This lineage runs directly to laptop production today

11-18.title: Delia Derbyshire realized the Doctor Who theme with tape
11-18.story: Working without synthesizers, Derbyshire built the theme by recording single tones, cutting the tape and splicing pitches by hand.
facts: Each note was measured with a ruler
She received no on-screen composer credit for years

11-19.title: Which 'Killing Me Softly' wins: Flack or the Fugees?
11-19.story: Roberta Flack's version is intimate and slow. The Fugees rebuilt it in 1996 over a hip-hop break with Lauryn Hill's lead.
facts: Flack publicly praised the remake
The Fugees kept the melody almost unchanged

11-20.title: Nile Rodgers' guitar is on more hits than you think
11-20.story: The Chic guitarist's clipped 'chucking' style powered his own band, then Bowie's 'Let's Dance', Madonna's 'Like a Virgin' and Daft Punk's 'Get Lucky'.
facts: He uses a 1960 Stratocaster he calls 'The Hitmaker'
He and Bernard Edwards wrote Sister Sledge's catalogue too

11-21.title: Which 'I Will Always Love You' wins: Dolly or Whitney?
11-21.story: Dolly Parton wrote it as a quiet goodbye to her mentor. Whitney Houston's 1992 version added the a cappella opening that producer David Foster fought for.
facts: Parton has said she cried hearing Whitney's version on the radio
The a cappella intro was nearly cut for being too risky

11-22.title: 'Apache' is called the national anthem of hip-hop
11-22.story: The Incredible Bongo Band's cover gave DJs a long percussion break perfect for cutting between two turntables.
facts: Kool Herc played it at Bronx block parties
The break is essentially a drum solo with congas

hits: LL Cool J - You Can't Dance

11-23.title: 'Change the Beat' gave the world its most-scratched sound
11-23.story: The 'ahhh, fresh' vocoder phrase at the end of Fab 5 Freddy's record became the single most-scratched sample in DJ history.
facts: It was recorded almost as an afterthought at the session's end
Nearly every turntablist routine still uses it

11-24.title: The Kings Theatre sat dark for 36 years
11-24.story: The Flatbush Avenue movie palace closed in 1977 and decayed with trees growing through the roof. A restoration reopened it in 2015 as one of Brooklyn's great music rooms.
facts: Original 1929 plasterwork was recast from surviving fragments
It now seats roughly 3,000 for concerts a mile from Ditmas Park

11-25.title: Dub was born by accident when a vocal track was left off
11-25.story: Engineer King Tubby pressed a version of a record with the vocals missing. Dancers loved it, so he began deliberately stripping tracks and drenching them in echo.
facts: He rewired mixing desks by hand to create his effects
Dub's remix logic is the direct ancestor of electronic dance music

11-26.title: Yoko Ono and John Lennon recorded a heartbeat
11-26.story: Their experimental albums included a recording of their unborn child's heartbeat, followed by silence after the pregnancy was lost. Few records have been that raw.
facts: Critics dismissed the work at the time
It anticipated decades of sound-art practice

11-27.title: Fats Domino sold more records than anyone but Elvis
11-27.story: The New Orleans pianist's rolling triplets defined early rock piano. He recorded almost everything at Cosimo Matassa's tiny J&M studio.
facts: The studio was in the back of an appliance shop
Its cramped room created the signature slapback sound

11-30.title: The Fairlight sampler cost as much as a house
11-30.story: The first commercial digital sampler sold for tens of thousands of dollars, limiting it to stars like Kate Bush and Peter Gabriel. It let musicians play any recorded sound from a keyboard.
facts: Bush used it to turn breaking glass into an instrument
Its low memory forced the short, clipped samples that define the era

12-01.title: Talking Heads built 'Remain in Light' from loops before loops existed
12-01.story: The band recorded single-bar grooves and spliced them into endless cycles by hand with razor blades and tape, inspired by Fela Kuti's Afrobeat.
facts: Each member recorded parts separately, never playing the song together
Eno and Byrne assembled the arrangements afterward

12-02.title: Prince Buster shaped the beat that became ska
12-02.story: Buster instructed guitarists to accent the offbeat, flipping Jamaican R&B into ska and eventually rocksteady and reggae.
facts: He staged sound-system clashes as public theatre
Two-tone bands in Britain rebuilt his catalogue

12-03.title: 'The Message' proved rap could report the news
12-03.story: Grandmaster Flash and the Furious Five released a bleak social document at a time when rap was expected to be party music.
facts: Most of the group disliked the song initially
Melle Mel delivers nearly all of it

12-04.title: Which 'Valerie' wins: The Zutons or Amy Winehouse?
12-04.story: The Zutons wrote it as indie rock. Mark Ronson and Amy Winehouse recut it as sixties soul, and that version eclipsed the original.
facts: Ronson built the arrangement around a Motown-style backbeat
Winehouse recorded her vocal quickly, largely live

12-05.title: Brooklyn's Celebrate Brooklyn keeps free music alive
12-05.story: The Prospect Park bandshell series has run for over four decades, one of the last major free festivals in New York.
facts: It draws crowds from across Flatbush and Ditmas Park
Many artists play it before headlining paid venues

12-06.title: Jay-Z grew up in Marcy Houses
12-06.story: Shawn Carter's Bed-Stuy childhood is stitched through his catalogue. Like Biggie, he famously records without writing lyrics down.
facts: He founded Roc-A-Fella after labels passed on signing him
Marcy Houses appears by name across three decades of his songs

12-07.title: The Ramones played 2:30 songs to fit more into a set
12-07.story: Their debut cost about $6,400 and ran under 30 minutes. Speed and brevity were economic decisions as much as aesthetic ones.
facts: They counted off every song identically
The whole album was recorded in about a week
